title: A separably closed coefficient field in a smooth strict localization
statement:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $Y$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] finite-type $K$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] of Krull dimension $d$ [def-kun-dimension]. For a geometric point $\bar y$ [def-weil-geometric-point] with image $y$, put $a=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(y)$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree], using the residue field [def-weil-residue-field] and $R=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Then $R$ is a regular local integral domain [def-weil-regular-scheme] of dimension $d-a$, its residue field is the chosen separable closure of $\kappa(y)$, and its fraction field is an algebraic extension of $K(Y)$ (the fraction field of the coordinate ring of any nonempty affine open of $Y$) via the structural embedding. There is a $K$-subfield $F\subset R$ which is separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed], such that reduction identifies $F$ with the residue field of $R$, and
$$\operatorname{trdeg}_K F=a,\qquad \operatorname{trdeg}_F\operatorname{Frac}(R)=d-a.$$

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $y$ with $A$ a finite type smooth $K$-algebra; such charts exist by the finite-type and affine-local smoothness conventions. Since $Y$ is integral, $A$ is a domain. Put $\mathfrak p=y\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $B=A_{\mathfrak p}$; the affine stalk localization identifies $B$ with $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, compatibly with germs and the residue-field map. Write $l$ for the separable closure of $\kappa(y)$ in the field of the geometric point.

source.place: Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), proof, choice of affine chart; affine-local smoothness in def-sbc-smooth-morphisms

proof.text: Identify the pointed-neighbourhood colimit defining $R$ with the algebraic strict henselization $B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ relative to $l$, as follows. In every affine pointed neighbourhood, the inverse image of $U$ contains its marked point; choose an affine open there containing that point. Thus neighbourhoods factoring through $U$ refine every neighbourhood, and the full-subcategory colimit lemma applies to the cofiltered system of the strict-local definition. For a neighbourhood over $U$, its residue field is finite separable over $\kappa(y)$, so its chosen image in the geometric-point field is contained in $l$. This verifies the hypothesis of the chart/residue-triples equivalence. Its natural ring isomorphism and the equivalence-colimit clause identify the colimit with the etale-residue-triples colimit over $(A,\mathfrak p,l)$. The localized-triples lemma gives this very colimit an $A_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra strict henselization structure, with unchanged structural map. The triples theorem therefore gives a surjective reduction $\rho:R\to l$, with kernel $\mathfrak m_R$, and says $R$ is henselian and $l$ separably closed.

source.place: Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), proof; Algebra Tags 04GW and 04GP via the cited triples statements

proof.text: The smooth-algebra regularity lemma makes $B$ a regular local ring, in particular Noetherian. Regularity is preserved by strict henselization, so $R$ is regular local. The regular-local-domain lemma makes $R$ an integral domain. Its structural map $B\to R$ is faithfully flat. It is injective: if $b$ maps to zero, the inclusion $bB\hookrightarrow B$ remains injective after flat tensoring with $R$, but its image is zero; faithfulness then forces $bB=0$, hence $b=0$. Consequently $A\hookrightarrow B\hookrightarrow R$ embeds $K(Y)=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ in $Q=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$.

For every nonempty open of $Y$ the integral locally-algebraic open-dimension lemma gives dimension $d$. By the definition of dimension at a point (minimum of neighbourhood dimensions), $\dim_yY=d$. Apply the finite-type point dimension formula: $d=\dim B+a$, so $0\le a\le d$ and $\dim B=d-a$. The strict-henselization dimension lemma gives $\dim R=\dim B=d-a$. At the generic point $\eta$ of $Y$, the closed-irreducible dimension/trdeg lemma with $C=|Y|$ gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_K K(Y)=d$; the affine stalk formula at the zero prime identifies $\kappa(\eta)$ with $\operatorname{Frac}(A)$.

The chart ind-etale lemma presents $R$ as a filtered colimit of etale $A$-algebras $C_i$. For $r\in R$, choose a representative $c\in C_i$ and put $\mathfrak q=\ker(C_i\to R\hookrightarrow Q)$. Its contraction to $A$ is zero by the injection just proved. Thus $C_i/\mathfrak q$ embeds in $Q$, and its fraction field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ embeds in $Q$. The etale-algebra residue-field lemma at this prime says $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is finite separable over $\kappa(0)=K(Y)$. In particular $r$ is algebraic over $K(Y)$. For a fraction $r/s\in Q$ choose a common stage representing $r$ and $s$ by filteredness. The same prime construction places $r/s$ in a finite separable residue field (the image of $s$ is nonzero). Hence $Q/K(Y)$ is algebraic; no injectivity of $C_i\to R$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), affine etale colimit; Algebra Tag 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field) via its cited residue-field consequence

proof.text: The residue field $\kappa(y)/K$ is finitely generated by the finite-type residue-field lemma applied to $K\to A$. As $K$ is algebraically closed, the separating-basis lemma gives $t_1,\ldots,t_a$ algebraically independent over $K$ with $\kappa(y)$ separable algebraic over $L=K(t_1,\ldots,t_a)$. Their number is $a$ by the transcendence-degree definition. Choose lifts $u_i\in R$ with $\rho(u_i)=t_i$. For every nonzero $P\in K[T_1,\ldots,T_a]$, $\rho(P(u))=P(t)\ne0$. Hence $P(u)$ is a unit in the local ring $R$, and evaluation uniquely extends to a $K$-embedding $j:L\hookrightarrow R$ whose reduction is the prescribed inclusion $L\subset l$. The empty basis gives $L=K$ by the same argument.

source.place: Proof, Local calculation in dimension d, first paragraph; Algebra Tag 030Z (lemma-perfect) via the separating-basis node

proof.text: The entire field $l$ is a separable closure of $L$, not merely a field containing one. To check this without choosing incompatible closures, let $M$ be the separable algebraic closure of $L$ inside $l$. The relative-closure statement says $M$ is a separably closed subfield. Every element of $\kappa(y)$ is separable algebraic over $L$, so $\kappa(y)\subseteq M$. For $z\in l$, its minimal polynomial over $\kappa(y)$ is separable. Over $M$ it remains separable, since its Bezout identity with its derivative remains valid; It splits into linear factors in $M$: choose a root using separable closedness and divide by its linear factor; the quotient is separable because a common factor of the quotient and its derivative would also divide the original polynomial and its derivative. Induction on degree finishes the factorization. Evaluating this factorization in the field $l$ forces $z$ to equal one of these roots in $M$. Thus $l=M$ and $l/L$ is separable algebraic and separably closed. In particular it is the directed union of its finite separable subextensions.

source.place: Proof, Local calculation in dimension d, first paragraph, choice of the separable closure; relative-closure statement from Fields Tags 09HC and 09HB

proof.text: For a finite subextension $E/L$ in $l$, choose a primitive element $\alpha$ by the primitive-element lemma. Its monic minimal polynomial $P\in L[T]$ is separable. Map the coefficients into $R$ by $j$; the residue polynomial is the original $P$ in $l[T]$, whose root $\alpha$ is simple: a Bezout identity $UP+VP'=1$ gives $V(\alpha)P'(\alpha)=1$. Since $R$ is henselian, the root-lifting lemma gives $v\in R$ with $P^j(v)=0$ and $\rho(v)=\alpha$. The evaluation map $L[T]\to E$ is surjective: $E=L(\alpha)$, and if $h(\alpha)\ne0$, irreducibility of $P$ gives $uh+vP=1$ for some $u,v\in L[T]$, hence $u(\alpha)=h(\alpha)^{-1}$. Thus $L[\alpha]=L(\alpha)$ and $E\cong L[T]/(P)$. Evaluation gives a unital $L$-algebra map $E=L[T]/(P)\to R$ sending $\alpha$ to $v$, because the kernel of evaluation $L[T]\to E$ is $(P)$. Its composite with $\rho$ is the inclusion $E\subset l$, so the map is injective. Denote it $s_E$.

source.place: Proof, Local calculation in dimension d, first paragraph, primitive elements and prescribed simple-root lifts; Fields Tag 030N and Algebra Tag 04GG

proof.text: These maps do not depend on the primitive-element choices and are compatible under inclusions. Indeed, for any $\beta\in E$, its monic minimal polynomial $P_\beta\in L[T]$ is separable. Any two $L$-algebra maps $E\to R$ reducing to $E\subset l$ send $\beta$ to roots of $P_\beta^j$ with the same residue $\beta$ and derivative a unit. The simple-root uniqueness lemma makes those two values equal, for every $\beta$. For $E\subset E'$, the restriction of $s_{E'}$ and $s_E$ have precisely these properties, hence agree. The directed union description of $l$ now defines a single ring map $s:l\to R$: set $s(z)=s_E(z)$ at any finite stage containing $z$. Given two elements, take a common finite stage; its ring-homomorphism laws give additivity and multiplicativity for $s$. One has $\rho s=\mathrm{id}_l$ and $s$ extends $j$.

source.place: Proof, Local calculation in dimension d, first paragraph, compatibility on finite subextensions; Algebra Tag 06RR (lemma-uniqueness)

proof.text: Set $F=s(l)\subset R$. Since $\rho s=\mathrm{id}_l$, $s$ is injective; its image is a subfield (the inverse of $s(z)$ for $z\ne0$ is $s(z^{-1})$), contains $K$, and reduction restricts to a field isomorphism $F\cong l$. Thus $F$ is separably closed: for a nonconstant separable polynomial $H=\sum c_iT^i\in F[T]$, apply $\rho|_F$ to its coefficients and to a Bezout identity for $H,H'$. The resulting nonconstant polynomial over $l$ is separable, so has a root $z\in l$. Since $s(\rho(c_i))=c_i$, applying $s$ to its vanishing at $z$ gives $H(s(z))=0$. The lifted family $u_1,\ldots,u_a$ is a transcendence basis of $F/K$, since it reduces to the basis and $F/j(L)\cong l/L$ is algebraic. Hence $\operatorname{trdeg}_KF=a$. The arbitrary geometric-point field has not been identified with $l$.

source.place: Proof, Local calculation in dimension d, first paragraph, the coefficient subfield and its residue identification

proof.text: Apply the transcendence-degree tower formula to $K\subset K(Y)\subset Q$: algebraicity of $Q/K(Y)$ gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_KQ=d$. Here the algebraic degree contributes zero because the empty family is a transcendence basis of an algebraic field extension. Apply the same formula to $K\subset F\subset Q$ to obtain $d=\operatorname{trdeg}_FQ+a$. Since $d$ and $a$ are finite and $a\le d$, this forces $\operatorname{trdeg}_FQ=d-a$. Together with the regularity, dimension and residue calculation, this proves every assertion.
